What We Do

Full-Service Optometry Revenue Cycle Management

Optometry billing requires precise routing between medical insurance for disease-related visits and vision insurance for routine refractive care. PMEX determines the correct payer and coverage category for every visit, and bills each claim through the right channel with the right codes.

Medical vs. Routine Vision Routing

Every visit categorized correctly: medical diagnosis to medical insurance, routine to vision plan.

Eye Exam Coding

92002 to 92014 coded by new/established status and complexity of the ocular evaluation.

Contact Lens Billing

Contact lens fitting (92310 to 92317) billed separately from the refraction service.

Glaucoma Management

Glaucoma evaluation and visual field testing (92083) billed to medical insurance.

Anti-VEGF Injection Billing

Bevacizumab, ranibizumab, and aflibercept J-codes billed with injection CPT and auth.

Diabetic Eye Exam Billing

Diabetic retinal exam (G0018, 92250) billed to medical insurance with correct ICD-10.

Sound Familiar?

Common Optometry Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Routine refraction billed to medical insurance and denied as non-covered.

PMEX routes refraction (92015) to the vision plan and medical diagnoses to medical insurance on every split-benefit visit.

Glaucoma visit sent to vision plan instead of medical insurance, underpaying the claim.

PMEX confirms the primary diagnosis for every visit and routes glaucoma, diabetic eye disease, and macular degeneration claims to medical insurance.

Anti-VEGF injection drug J-code quantity not verified against the administered dose.

PMEX verifies the drug quantity from the injection record and bills the correct J-code units on every intravitreal injection claim.

Contact lens fitting billed as part of the comprehensive exam, bundling revenue incorrectly.

PMEX bills contact lens fitting codes separately from the eye exam on every fitting encounter.

Visual field test not billed alongside the glaucoma management visit.

PMEX identifies visual field testing from the visit documentation and submits 92083 alongside the glaucoma E/M on qualifying visits.

Prior authorization not obtained for anti-VEGF injections, triggering retroactive denial.

PMEX manages anti-VEGF prior authorization and tracks renewal windows per patient per injection cycle.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Optometry Billing

Optometry practices lose 16 to 26 percent of revenue to medical vs. routine routing errors, anti-VEGF auth gaps, and refraction bundling mistakes.

PATTERN 01

Glaucoma Visit Routed to Vision Plan

Glaucoma suspect evaluation billed to vision insurance. Denied as medical diagnosis. Vision plan does not cover disease management. Medical insurance was the correct payer. Revenue lost for the visit and the visual field test billed alongside it.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX categorizes every visit by primary diagnosis before submission. Glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, macular degeneration, and other disease diagnoses are routed to medical insurance on the date of service.

PATTERN 02

Anti-VEGF Injection Denied, Authorization Expired

Aflibercept intravitreal injection administered. Commercial authorization expired 3 weeks prior. Renewal not initiated. Drug claim ($1,850) and injection administration ($145) both denied. Retroactive auth not available.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks anti-VEGF authorization expiration per patient and initiates renewal 14 days before the next scheduled injection, with clinical documentation of treatment response attached to the renewal request.

PATTERN 03

Refraction Billed to Medical Insurance and Denied

Comprehensive eye exam billed to medical insurance. 92015 (refraction) included on the medical claim. Medical insurance denies refraction as a routine vision service not covered under the medical benefit. $45 per visit denied.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX splits eye exam billing between medical and vision payers on every visit with both a medical diagnosis and a refraction. Refraction is billed to the vision plan and disease management services to medical insurance.

Questions

Optometry Billing Questions Answered

We categorize every service by benefit type. Medical diagnoses such as glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, and macular degeneration are billed to medical insurance. Refractions and contact lens fittings are billed to the vision plan.

Refraction (92015) is not covered by most medical insurance plans and is billed to the vision plan or as a self-pay service. We confirm the coverage structure before billing each visit.

We bill the drug J-code at the correct quantity from the injection record, the injection administration CPT code (67028), and confirm prior authorization is active before the injection is administered.

Yes. Contact lens fitting codes (92310 to 92317) are billed separately from the comprehensive eye exam. We confirm the fitting documentation supports the specific code before submission.

Yes. Diabetic retinal exams with documented diabetic retinopathy or diabetic eye disease are covered under medical insurance. We apply the correct ICD-10 and CPT codes for medical billing.
